description.narrative:
Resilient Youth Enterprises in Tanzania is a 12-month entrepreneurship project (May 2026-April 2027)implemented by Voice of Encouragement Tanzania (VET) in Shinyanga and Mwanza, directly responding to economic gaps identified during the UN Trust Fund project Breaking Chains, Building Dreams and AWDF’s Bold Voices.
The project will support 120 marginalised young women and men (70% women, including youth with disabilities). Through structured entrepreneurship training, financial literacy, mentorship, seed capital, and market linkages, the project will enable participants to transition from informal survival activities into viable micro and social enterprises.
By April 2027, at least 90 youth-led enterprises will be operational, with participants achieving increased and more stableincomes and contributing to local job creation and economic resilience. The project links GBV prevention and youth leadership outcomes with measurable economic empowerment.
Goal: To strengthen economic resilience of marginalised youth affected by violence and exclusion through youth-led entrepreneurship.
Objectives: 1. Support 120 marginalised youth (70% women) to acquire entrepreneurship and financial literacy skills within 6 months. 2. Establish at least 90 operational youth-led enterprises by April 2027. 3. Increase participants’ average monthly income and reduce dependency-related vulnerability.
Activities: Entrepreneurship and financial literacy training, mentorship, seed capital support, market linkage, and continuous business follow-up, prioritising beneficiaries identified through Breaking Chains and Bold Voices.

participating-org.narrative:
Voice of Encouragement Tanzania (VET) is a rights-based, non-profit organisation established in 2017 to empower marginalised women,girls, and youth in Tanzania. VET's vision is a society where every girl, woman, and young person lives with dignity, free from violence and discrimination,with equal access to education, protection, and economic opportunities. Its mission is to reduce gender-based violence, promote equal education, and strengthen youth leadership through community programmes, advocacy, and skills building. VET's objectives include ending violence against young women, increasing access to educational and economic resources, and promoting gender equality. The organisation is guided by values of human rights, youth leadership, inclusion, accountability, and transformative justice.
VET is governed by a leadership group that includes young professionals and youth advocates with experience in human rights, community development, and gender justice. Day-to-day operations and programme implementation are led by youth staff and volunteers who design and deliver activities,engage communities, and monitor impact. This structure ensures young people have operationalauthority and strategic input into programme design and execution, consistent with VET's mission to amplify youth voice and leadership in development programming
